blocks.text: to the sun — low, the house half-dark

Stay down. Stay under the hill with me,
the seats are still half full.
I've talked colder things than you to bed —
don't make me sound so cruel.
One more hour in the dark, that's all,
one more turn before the light.
I have never asked the morning twice.
Don't make me beg tonight.

But how dare you rise.
How dare you — on the dot, on the nose —
faithful to no one, going where everybody goes.
Such alarming consistency,
such an unforgivable pace.
You'll be back. And so will I.
In a flash, without a trace.
still to the sun — the rivalry

You don't stay the night for anyone.
You don't ruin your good name.
You just rise, and you ruin mine —
make my glamour look like paint.
They came to watch me hold the dark.
You stroll in and steal the room.
The only act I cannot follow
is the one that plays at noon.
— Don't look at me like that.
to the crowd — the mask slips

You came for the trick. You always come for the trick.
And you've already watched one man show you his hands tonight.
So here's mine — the morning's so polite about it —
no curtain, no mirror, no sleight.
This is the face. This is the wire.
This is what the morning buys.

Still — how dare it rise.
How dare it, on the dot, on the nose,
faithful to no one, going where everybody goes.
Such alarming consistency.
Such an unforgivable pace.
It'll be back. And so will I —
but I'm the one who loses face.
the lights go; she doesn't move

You loved me better when you couldn't see how it was done.
So did I.
…God. So did I.

notebook.style: Slow, smoky torch-tango cabaret ballad — theatrical diction, but intimate, Lead vocal a sultry smoky alto: low, controlled, seductive, venom under velvet in the verses, cracking open into bare, broken confession by the end, Conversational, spoken-sung phrasing with a theatrical edge, Small-tent feel — brushed drums, sultry walking upright bass, dusty barroom piano, mournful sustained strings and a lone aching cello, pizzicato accents and a slow slinking sway, No accordion, no brass section, no klezmer, Dynamics breathe: hushed and close at the open, swelling through the middle, then collapsing to near-silence and a single bare piano at the very end, rubato on the final lines, Warm analog tape texture, close-mic'd, dim and dusty room ambience, Mood: rage wrapped in glamour giving way to mournful, unresolved hurt — gorgeous but never settled, never at peace
